title: After Jazz Limited: jobbing and illness

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: After Jazz Limited closed, where were you working next?
Well, I was mostly jobbing, and like I worked Jazz Five. at
That's right.
And the In Place on Sundays.
With Jerry?
With Jerry Fuller.
That's right.
I did that until I got sick and went in the hospital.
When was that?
Must have been somewhere around '73, I guess, or '74.
Yeah, I remember when you first went in.
Jazz Limited closed in what, '72?
Yeah.

And I did a lot of gigging, with Art Hodes, Bill Tinkley. And I did that until the very fine president of the Gas Light Band would hire me on Sundays. He was working at Alfred's. That's when I started with Joe Kelly.
Johnny Board's in that band now. Was he --
He was in the band, yeah.
Who was in it? Barrett Deems on drums?
Yeah, and Larry on saxophone, from Czechoslovakia. And Joe Kelly, he was a real -- Michael
Fuller on piano. That was the band when I started.
When did you go into the Gaslight Club?

I went into the Gaslight Club shortly after that. I went in there to make an album with Joe Kelly. And then he finally persuaded Mr. Brown, Burton Brown, to put the bass on. So that's when I started at the Gaslight.
When was that?
This is '77, and I was there five years --
'72. Yeah, that was '72 when I started with him. At the Gaslight.
